Bad messages: parent `1791809110.099659`, thread reply `1791809110.387019` (C03CGTN3KN1). Joshua needs to delete both (the bot can't).
- **Root cause (checked against the files, not metadata):** `monday_pull.sh` pulled End of Month for 10/1..10/11 (Sunday) at 06:14. Bravo returned a **degenerate export**: right `Reporting Dates` header, but no daily rows, a blank `Total:` row, every Loan Base cell 0, Layaway block 0, and the Inventory Base day columns collapsed (3 values instead of 4). `store_rankings.py` reads by position, so it took inventory index 2 (= month QTY) as dollars and got $0 loans, $0 service charges and $0 layaway. Its only completeness check was "5 files exist, >=500 bytes", so it posted. ceo_week_pull's 07:44 and 07:56 re-pulls of 10/5..10/11 and 10/1..10/11 came back degenerate the same way, so this is Bravo's output for that window that morning, not a one-off file write. The Saturday-stamped 10/1..10/10 set (written Sun 21:43–22:07) is clean. The 10/1..10/4 Monday pull on 10/5 was also clean, so this failure comes and goes. It was not the canonical-copy logic, and the report window was right.
- **Fix (backups `fleet/_backups/{store_rankings,monday_compile}.py.bak-pre-sanity-20261012`):** `store_rankings.py` gets `validate()`: window = 1st..END; Ending Loan and Inventory Base rows have 4 numbers with day == month and > 0; `Total:` row not blank. An invalid set is skipped for the next older valid one (labelled with its own date). If none is valid: HOLD, exit 2, ledger row. Then `sanity()` withholds (exit 2 + ledger row) on any store with $0 loans or $0 inventory, $0 company service charges, or a >50% store or company loan/inventory drop vs the prior week's valid set (end-5..9 days). It tests clean on the 10/11 files (would have withheld on 18 counts) and passes on 10/4 and 10/10. New `--prefix TEXT` puts TEXT before the summary. `monday_compile.py` now tells Joshua's rollup DM that a sanity-gate hold was WITHHELD and why, instead of "held until complete".
- **Corrected post:** rendered on the Mac (identical to sandbox), checked against the 10/10 workbooks (loan, inventory, layaway, Total: row and Sales Revenue (Profit) cells read directly) and against last week (company loans $736,774.98 -> $734,207.88, inventory $724,158.77 -> $735,113.45). Retail, scrap and profit in the 10/10 and 10/11 files are identical, so stores were closed Sunday and 10/10 is the full week. Posted as Goldilocks: `1791821054.326109` ("Corrected: ... Report Period: 2026-10-10"), with the thread broadcast `1791821054.774469`.
- **10/5 post was NOT affected:** its figures match the 10/4 workbooks to the penny (loans $736,774.98).
- **#ffl-transfer-performance 09:54:17 (`1791813257.553729`) was NOT empty.** Raw `conversations.history` (new read-only `vp_slack.py raw <ch> <ts>`, backup `vp_slack.py.bak-pre-rawcmd-20261012`) shows a native Slack table block with all 5 stores plus the Total. The `text` fallback has them too. The Slack connector/reader (and clients that don't support table blocks) show only the title and summary line. Every figure checked against the five 10/1..10/12 nics-transfers CSVs: CUL $260/11, ROA $70/4, WAY $50/2, HAR $25/1, LEX $25/1, total $430/19. No repost. ## 2026-10-09 (open-error fixes)

- **Jewelry nightly 10/8 (CUL/HAR/LEX/WAY missing) — root cause: a self-inflicted watcher-restart storm, not the v3 handler.** `bravo_run` (bin/vp_lib.sh) "self-healed" (restarted the VM watcher) whenever its OWN trigger sat unclaimed >180 s — but the watcher is serial, so any trigger queued behind a running one hit that. `_restart_watcher_v2.log` shows 60+ restarts 21:17 (10/8) → 08:32 (10/9), and every jewelry run that died did so seconds after one (CUL 02:43:39, LEX 02:44:43, WAY 02:55:53, HAR 06:15:41, CUL 07:04, CUL 08:32:33 …). A killed claim is never re-run, so CSVs never landed (the CSV is written only after all 8 categories). The overnight pm-loan-growth flood (~85 triggers from 20:00) pushed the 20:43 jewelry jobs to 02:37 and multiplied the waiters. Second collision: `bravo_pull.sh`'s pre-pull health gate ran recover-to-dashboard (a separate AHK driving Bravo's screen) under a live run (10/9 08:27 during CUL), because `bravo_busy` reads the claim file's mtime (= claim time) and so calls a 10-min run "not busy" after 3 min. The ledger's "claimed backlog 18" was orphaned claims, not a queue. v3 handler itself is fine: when not killed, WAY (08:46) and CUL (09:18, 8/8 incl. the 19/19 dup-verify) completed.
  - **Fix (additive, backups `fleet/_backups/vp_lib.sh.bak-pre-selfheal-busy-20261009`, `bravo_pull.sh.bak-pre-selfheal-busy-20261009`):** new `bravo_active <min> [skip-id]` = a trigger in `triggers/claimed` whose own log was written in the last N min (same per-trigger scoping as `_watchdog.ps1`'s 2026-08-04 in-flight fix). `bravo_run` now DEFERS its self-heal while another trigger is active (logs "self-heal deferred …", resets its clock, keeps its one heal), and re-queues its own trigger once if it was orphaned. `VP_SELFHEAL_LEGACY=1` restores the old behaviour. `bravo_pull.sh` skips the health gate while the watcher is mid-run ("health gate skipped: watcher mid-run on …"). Same guard added to the two scripts that carried their own copy of the rule: `monday_pull.sh` (unclaimed-3-min self-heal) and `morning_pull.sh` (STEP 2 unconditional "watcher hygiene" restart + its STEP 5 self-heal) — backups `fleet/_backups/{monday,morning}_pull.sh.bak-pre-selfheal-busy-20261009`; both `bash -n` clean, not yet exercised live (next morning pull Sat 10/10, Monday pull 10/12).
  - **Verified live 08:52–09:24:** retry4 CUL/HAR/LEX waiters logged 13 deferrals instead of restarts while discount-review (08:50, a production daily report) and CUL ran; LEX skipped the gate during discount-review; CUL jewelry 10/8 completed 8/8 `success` (09:18:50), then HAR (09:31) and LEX (09:49) back to back with zero watcher restarts after 09:05 — all five 10/8 CSVs are now on disk (ROA 06:42, WAY 08:46). No AHK handler, saved report or watcher dispatch line was touched.
  - Unchanged / still open: HAR Charms, WAY Charms, LEX Charms+Brooches return no row total (empty categories, standing since 8/2x) — v3 records them as `error`, never 0, as designed; each costs ~5 min of polling per store. **Tonight 10/9:** `_hold_pmlg_overnight` holds 57 pm-loan-growth jobs named `20261009-2000-*`; if released at 20:00 they sort ahead of the 20:43 jewelry jobs again (delay, no longer kills).

Verified: `field_scorecard.py --dry-run` → `daily-funds-verification | OK | Thu 10/08 18:00`.
